title: Schema-driven telemetry sanitization, provenance tagging, and RBAC access logs
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Implement a schema-driven sanitization engine for telemetry (logs, traces, metrics) that tags fields with data-sensitivity provenance at ingestion, applies redaction/pseudonymization transforms according to tenant policies, and generates RBAC-scoped access logs. The goal is to provide deterministic, auditable scrubbing with minimal downstream breakage, allow retention TTL enforcement per-tenant/field, and retain lineage for debugging while meeting compliance requirements.
acceptance_criteria: A JSON-schema-based rule registry exists in Consul/ConfigStore and can be updated via console UI and API
Ingestion hooks for logs and traces apply redaction transforms per rule and attach a provenance header with hashed token and rule id
Retention TTLs applied at the storage layer enforce per-field/tenant expiration and are visible in the console
RBAC-scoped access logs record each read/unmask request with user, role, resource, timestamp, and justification token
End-to-end tests exercise common PII patterns (emails, credit card, SSNs) and demonstrate no unredacted samples in tenant scope
tasks: Design schema registry format and rules language (json-schema + redact directives)
Add tracing hooks in the ingestion pipeline to inspect and tag events before batching
Implement streaming sanitizer service with transform cache and KMS-backed pseudonymization
Add retention enforcement layer to s3/gcs partition writer and indexer
Expose rule editor and provenance viewer in Console; link to incident playbooks
Instrument metrics and dashboard for false-positive/negative rates and added latency
Write migration/safety strategy and rollout plan with canary and kill-switch
decisions: Use JSON Schema extension for field-level sensitivity instead of freeform regex rules to reduce false positives
Pseudonymization will use HMAC with tenant-specific key from KMS to preserve deterministic linking across events
Default behavior is redaction (masking) with explicit allowlist for fields that can be stored in plaintext
Retention enforcement will be handled at storage indexer rather than downstream query layer for stronger guarantees
progress_updates: 2025-11-14: Kickoff meeting with security, infra, and console teams. Drafted rule language and initial registry schema.
2025-11-21: Infra spike showed added latency of ~3ms/event in unoptimized sanitizer; agreed to add transform cache and sampling for hot paths.
2025-11-30: First ingestion hook prototype landed (PR #58). Manual test showed provenance header attached for trace spans.
2025-12-02: Design review with PM and Security. Security requested KMS HMAC approach and explicit audit trail format; accepted with action items.
2025-12-03: QA started on canary tenant with synthetic PII dataset. Initial dashboard shows 0.7% false positives flagged for review.
risks_mitigation: Risk: Over-scrubbing breaks downstream parsers. Mitigation: Provide allowlist and field-preservation mode plus schema-versioned rules and canary rollouts.
Risk: Performance regression in ingest path. Mitigation: Batch-aware sanitizer, transform cache, and selective sampling for low-risk tenants.
Risk: Audit log volume growth. Mitigation: Rollup summaries for common read patterns and configurable retention for access logs.
Risk: Tenant keys compromise. Mitigation: KMS-backed keys with rotation; store only HMAC tokens, not raw pseudonyms.
qa_plan: Create synthetic datasets covering 20+ PII permutations; run ingestion against canary and assert no plaintext in tenant-scoped storage
Inject load test to measure 99th percentile latency impact and ensure SLOs met with autoscaling
Run red-team to attempt exfiltration via allowed fields and verify RBAC logs capture intent
